newsitem.title: USA: Final phase of Food Lion lawsuit delayed.
newsitem.headline: Final phase of Food Lion lawsuit delayed.

text.p: The third and final phase of grocery store chain Food Lion Inc's lawsuit against the ABC television network was postponed until January 6, when jurors will begin hearing evidence on punitive damages, the grocer said in a statement.
The jury was due to return to the courtroom on January 3, but U.S. District Court Judge N. Carlton Tilley granted a postponement to allow attorneys for both sides more time to prepare their cases.
Food Lion sued ABC and four producers of its newsmagazine show "PrimeTime Live" for a 1992 program that claimed the grocer sold old food and repackaged out-of-date merchandise.

Salisbury, N.C.-based Food Lion charged fraud, deceptive trade practices, conspiracy and breach of duty of loyalty against the ABC producers working undercover at two Food Lion stores. It argued that while the producers were employed by the store they were obligated to ensure sanitary practices.

On Monday, the jury found New York-based ABC, a unit of Walt Disney Co, and its producers had committed fraud, trespass and breach of employee loyalty in the undercover investigation and awarded the grocer $1,402 in actual damages.
Food Lion had sought $2,432.35 in order to cover the wages paid to the two producers working undercover plus the company's costs to train them.

It said it plans to argue for more in punitive damages and will call as an expert witness E. Robert Lissit, an associate professor of broadcast journalism at the S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications at Syracuse University in New York.
